text.p: Stocks drifted higher Tuesday as profit-taking put a damper on the market's rebound from last week's shakeout.

At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 11.71 points at 6,567.62 after Monday's gain of 30 points and Friday's leap of 49 points, which came on the heels of a plunge of nearly 215 points last week.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a small margin on active New York Stock Exchange volume of 246 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index, which is laced with technology stocks, was up 2.26 points at 1,253.61.
"Typically, when a market starts to rally from its lows, the first rally is not a very good one. That's standard procedure," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross.

"We have not made a bottom. We had had a trading low," Blumberg said. "This is a recovery which will last a few days, but not more than that. It's led by techs, and usually after a correction like the one they have had, you rotate into another group. I think we will restest the lows next week."

Since late on Friday, technology stocks have led the market's rebound from last week's sell-off, and the sector got further impetus after the release of better-than-forecast earnings from Advanced Micro Devices Inc.
Advanced Micro was up 2-1/2 at 43-3/4. Intel Corp. rose 5/8 to 145-3/4, Microsoft Corp. was up 9/16 at 145-11/16 and International Business Machines Corp. gained 2-3/4 at 135.

"The worst is probably over for the techs, but this is not the group that will lead us higher," Blumberg said. "That will be the role of either the consumer non-durables or energy stocks. People tend to get defensive after a sell-off and consumer non-durables have earnings consistency and the energy sector has gotten washed out."
Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons, said technology stocks still remained the best bet for long-term investors.

"The techs are saying that they are the place to be in a bounce. Long-term investors are chasing earnings, and I don't know of any group that has better earnings prospects for the remainder of this decade," he said.
Goldman said the overall Dow Jones index was undergoing a recovery from its lows and that it had another 100 to 125 points higher to go.
"The important thing is that we are still seeing a correction in a bull market," he said.
Among individual stocks, Motorola Inc. fell 5/8 to 59-5/8 despite the company's beating first quarter earnings estimates as analysts said the technology giant's outlook was positive but cautious.
Transocean Offshore Inc. stock was up 2-1/2 at 61-3/8. The company said it received letters-of-intent to contract two of its modern deepwater drilling rigs.
Viking Office Products Inc. fell 5-1/2 to 14-1/2 after warning of disappointing earnings for the latest quarter.
